provider_query: 过去 48 小时内关于半导体出口管制的一条新闻
answer:
过去约48小时内，最直接相关的一条新闻是：SK海力士把在美国建厂与放宽对华设备出口挂钩。

**主新闻（路透，2026年10月14日报道）**  
SK海力士正寻求华盛顿批准，向其中国大连厂出口更多美国芯片制造设备以扩产，并以此作为在美国建厂的条件。消息人士称，其美国子公司Solidigm希望在大连闲置空间安装新设备生产NAND。美国商务部此前对在华现有晶圆厂发放有限许可，但一般不批准扩产或技术升级用设备；2025年12月对大连厂的2026年许可也对设备数量有限制。背景是美国限制对华芯片设备出口，以延缓中国先进半导体（含AI与军事用途）发展。  
来源：Reuters，2026-10-14/15。  
[[1]](https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/sk-***/)

**相关近况（最多约8条，简明出处）**

1. **SK海力士以赴美设厂换设备出口许可** — 同上，路透独家，2026-10-14。  
   [[1]](https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/sk-***/)

2. **中文媒体跟进同一消息** — 中时等称SK海力士以赴美兴建NAND厂为条件，争取批准更多美制设备出口大连。中时新闻网，2026-10-15。  
   [[2]](https://www.chinatimes.com/search/%e5%87%ba%e5%8f%a3%e7%ae%a1%e5%88%b6)

3. **英伟达在华AI芯片份额下滑** — IDC称2026年上半年英伟达中国数据中心AI芯片份额降至约34%（2025年约55%），华为升至约28%；报道将此与美国出口管制限制供货联系起来。路透/中时，约2026-10-13至14。  
   [[2]](https://www.chinatimes.com/search/%e5%87%ba%e5%8f%a3%e7%ae%a1%e5%88%b6)

4. **SEMI警告单边出口管制** — SEMI致信特朗普，警告拟议中针对华为的外国直接产品规则与微量规则修订可能冲击美企与全球供应链。EMSNow转载SEMI，页面日期2026-10-15（文内事件时间更早）。  
   [[3]](https://www.emsnow.com/semi-warns-against-new-unilateral-u-s-export-controls-on-commercial-technology/)

5. **先进芯片出口与关税政策回顾** — 分析称商务部将部分H200/MI325X级芯片对华出口由推定拒绝改为个案审查，并配合对相关进口加征25%第232条关税（规则时间点在文中为2026年1月）。EMSNow，页面2026-10-15。  
   [[4]](https://www.emsnow.com/a-mixed-bag-of-chips-significant-new-import-and-export-changes-for-advanced-semiconductors/)

6. **阿斯麦对华设备销售仍高** — 南华早报称尽管美国推动收紧出口限制，阿斯麦对华芯片设备销售大增，并预计中国约占其今年销售的20%。SCMP专题页，2026-10-15前后。  
   [[5]](https://www.scmp.com/topics/semiconductors-geopolitics)

7. **光模块/PCB“管制”传闻被澄清** — 多家中文财经报道称近期市场把政府采购提案、FCC新规与国防采购限制混为一谈；并非已落地的对华全面出口管制。财联社/新浪等，2026-10-15。  
   [[6]](https://finance.sina.com.cn/jjxw/2026-10-15/doc-inivhier8104271.shtml)

8. **美国计划将芯片关税豁免与本地生产挂钩** — 韩媒称华盛顿或按类似对台模式，把关税豁免与在美产能挂钩，施压三星、SK海力士加大美国投资。Korea JoongAng Daily，约2026-10-8（略早于48小时，作背景）。  
   [[7]](https://www.koreajoongangdaily.com/business/planned-us-chip-tariffs-to-tie-exemptions-to-local-production-pressure-korea-to-invest-more/12908571)

**说明：** 检索结果里部分页面显示“Published: 2026-10-15”，但正文日期可能是更早旧闻被重新抓取；上面第1–3条最符合“过去约48小时”的半导体出口管制新闻。

results.title: U.S. uncovers scheme to reroute Nvidia GPUs worth $160 million to China despite export bans - CNBC
results.snippet: # U.S. uncovers scheme to reroute Nvidia GPUs worth $160 million to China despite export bans. * Two Chinese men were detained for allegedly smuggling Nvidia chips to China and other restricted locations. U.S. authorities announced Tuesday that they have shut down yet another China-linked smuggling network that trafficked or attempted to traffic more than $160 million in export-controlled Nvidia AI chips. The case comes as Washington steps up its enforcement of export controls aimed at curbing China's access to advanced AI technologies, including Nvidia's Graphics Processing Units. Officials said Hsu and associates had exported or attempted to export at least $160 million worth of Nvidia H100 and H200 GPUs between October 2024 and May 2025. Both allegedly conspired independently with a Hong Kong logistics company and a China-based AI firm to evade chip controls. The investigation involved the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry and Security, which oversees and enforces U.S. export controls, including those on Nvidia.

results.title: Taiwanese Authorities Raid Supermicro Amid Nvidia Chip Probe - Let's Data Science
results.snippet: Editorial analysis: For AI infrastructure teams and procurement leads, expanded export-control enforcement in Taiwan increases compliance risk and could complicate supply chains for high-end accelerators. Reported facts: Bloomberg reports Taiwanese investigators raided **Super Micro Computer** offices in Taiwan on June 29 as part of a widening probe into alleged smuggling of **Nvidia** chips to China. Bloomberg and Investing.com report the Keelung District Prosecutors Office searched six residences and three affiliated companies. The Next Web and Investing.com report that Taiwan currently does not criminalize AI chip exports to China but is reportedly considering making such exports a crime. According to Bloomberg and Investing.com, Taiwan's Keelung District Prosecutors Office searched six residences and the sites of three affiliated companies. **Reported legal and policy details** Investing.com and Yahoo/Investing report that Taiwan does not currently classify AI chip exports to China as a criminal offense, and that prosecutors have relied on other statutes such as document forgery in earlier cases.
